kata.name: probe granularity re-score of the bogart pilot: the kw9.3 lint stays silent on a faithful re-model of pilot model 1 — precision 2/69 becomes 0 findings, ratio undefined; rule NOT validated
kata.series_verdict: pre-registered decision rule: a better real/noise ratio than 2/69 requires a defined ratio; zero findings make it undefined (0 real, 0 noise) — the rule is NOT validated on this second domain, the docs label stays PROPOSED, and the measurement including the recall cost is attached as the negative result

expected.detail: sampled drop audit of the pilot's noise source: the derived arrow `hit_edition_date` (read_pages→edition_date, derived in read_service, no storing column) and the tautological equation `document_id ; edition_date = hit_edition_date` — the pre-registered expectation was that the lint flags the derived arrow as an over-constraint instead of emitting the 67 noise findings

the pilot's two real findings (bogart-4wt selector ambiguity, still present per the 2026-11-13 live census: nacional/primera 2026-11-03 and pba/JUDICIAL 2026-11-03) are structurally excluded — backfill_captures / backfill_partitions store no selector→capture column; recorded as the recall cost / named gap, never papered over

commands: target/debug/catherine check fixtures/probes/granularity-bogart/pilot-model.ct.json --json # exit 0, data.findings [], constraints_checked 1, rows_evaluated 8 (no --granularity flag exists; the lint rides the shared check path)

comparison.conventional_baseline: The bogart pilot itself (catherine-hc6, models 1–3): 69 findings, 2 real / 67 noise (2.9% real). The pilot is a committed recorded result, not a re-executed arm on this fixture, so no baseline-arm uniqueness claim is made; unique_detections is empty.

expressibility_gap.why: the storage-granularity rule's model cannot express the only real defects the pilot ever found on this system: backfill_captures / backfill_partitions store no selector→capture column, so neither the 2 real nor the 67 noise pilot findings are expressible as model findings. Derivation and selection claims must be declared and checked by the rule-lens / policy machinery, not suppressed by the granularity rule.

discrepancies: the kw9.4 assignment pre-registered that the lint would flag `hit_edition_date` as an over-constraint (exit 3); the executed run falsifies that expectation — with 3 arrows over 8 rows the cap gate (ceil(4.5·√8) = 13) never trips, so the lint fires nothing and the exit is 0. The honest observation is recorded, not the pre-registered one.
procedure: 1. The drop audit: fixtures/probes/granularity-bogart/pilot-model.ct.json re-models pilot model 1 (catherine-hc6, model1_fts_anchor.ct.json) exactly as the README's dropped section describes — arrow `document_id` as a single column (the real reference is composite), derived arrow `hit_edition_date` (no storing column), and the tautological equation; tiny consistent instance (3 documents / 4 pages / 1 edition).
2. The check arm ran on the fixture: exit 0 with zero findings — the lint does not fire at this shape (cap-gated; the pre-registered expectation of a fired finding was falsified; see discrepancies).
3. Elements compared at fault level against the pilot's recorded 69 findings: nothing is detected by the lint, so unique_detections is empty and no uniqueness claim is made.

4. The pre-registered decision rule (README, fixed 2026-11-13): zero findings make the real/noise ratio undefined, so the rule is NOT validated on this domain; the docs label stays PROPOSED. The 2 real findings' structural exclusion is the recall cost, recorded as a named gap.

5. Verdict killed: the probe fired nothing on faults the series predicted (the noise source is neither flagged nor the pilot findings reproduced). The null result is the deliverable, never suppressed.
